think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 70-year-old male presents with multiple small subcutaneous nodules on the right forearm with a prior history of unilateral forearm weakness 4 years earlier. The clinical presentation mimics common benign mesenchymal tumors, rheumatoid nodules, or indolent bacterial furunculosis, masking an unrecognized peripheral nerve involvement with erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL).
2. Admission Breakpoint: The breakpoint occurs after initial physical examination and history taking, strictly prior to fine-needle aspiration (FNA) cytology and acid-fast staining.
3. Differential Distinctions: Benign subcutaneous lipomas or fibromas lack acute inflammatory cells, histiocytic foamy macrophages, or granulomatous changes. Pyogenic bacterial soft-tissue abscesses yield purulent aspirates with identifiable bacteria on Gram stain and positive routine cultures.
case_prompt:
A 70-year-old male presented to the outpatient clinic with localized swellings on his right forearm. On clinical inquiry, he noted a previous history of focal motor weakness involving the right forearm four years earlier, which had not been definitively evaluated. He had no fever, systemic constitutional symptoms, or active skin ulceration.

On physical examination, the vital signs were within normal limits. Examination of the right upper extremity revealed multiple small, discreet subcutaneous nodular swellings along the right forearm, the largest of which measured 0.8 cm × 0.6 cm. The nodules were firm and mobile, without overlying ulceration. A general examination revealed no generalized lymphadenopathy.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Subacute pyogenic soft-tissue infection or bacterial furunculosis
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the presence of multiple inflammatory subcutaneous nodules, but both Gram stain and bacterial cultures were negative for pyogenic pathogens.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: In both the cases, Gram's stain and bacterial culture were performed which came out as negative.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Benign mesenchymal neoplasms or rheumatoid nodules
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered given the indolent presentation and localized nodular morphology in an elderly male, but cytological evaluation demonstrated a dense polymorphous inflammatory infiltrate with foamy macrophages, eosinophils, and epithelioid granuloma formation rather than bland adipocytic/fibrous tissue or necrobiotic granulomas.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The WG stained smears showed dense mixed inflammatory cell infiltrate comprising polymorphs, foamy macrophages, eosinophils, and lymphoid cells. Few of the macrophages were present in clusters and showed epithelioid transformation forming ill-formed granulomas.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: In a patient with antecedent focal upper extremity neuropathy, fine-needle aspiration yielding granulomatous and neutrophilic inflammation with positive Fite staining for lepra bacilli definitively established erythema nodosum leprosum (Type 2 lepra reaction).
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: FNA was performed which yielded granular aspirate. The WG stained smears showed dense mixed inflammatory cell infiltrate comprising polymorphs, foamy macrophages, eosinophils, and lymphoid cells. ... Fite stain for lepra bacilli was positive [Figure 2].

editor_comments: This case highlights the subtle presentation of leprosy and Type 2 reaction (ENL) manifesting as asymptomatic or mildly tender subcutaneous forearm nodules associated with prior mononeuropathy, confirmed cytologically by FNA and Fite staining.
